newsitem.title: YEMEN: World Bank allocates new loans to Yemen.
newsitem.headline: World Bank allocates new loans to Yemen.

text.p: The World Bank has allocated $420 million in new loans to Yemen over a three year period on the condition that the Arab state keeps up its faster pace of project implementation, a World Bank official said on Wednesday.

At the end of a six-day visit to Sanaa, the Bank's Middle East and North Africa Director Inder Sud told a news conference the Bank had "decided to allocate $420 million as loans to Yemen for the coming three fiscal years 1997, 1998 and 1999".
The visit -- during which he met President Ali Abdullah Saleh and other senior officials -- was Sud's third since the Bank opened an office in Sanaa in 1995.

"If the competence improvement of project implementation continues, the whole amount will be made available to the Yemeni authorities...otherwise a reconsideration of the $420 million will take place," Sud said.
The World Bank had previously complained that Yemen had been slow in implementing projects financed through soft loans it had provided. But Sud said things had recently improved.
"Currently we recorded a good progress for implementation of projects thanks to measures undertaken by the government during the last period," he said.

The Bank also planned to extend aid to Yemen to deal with flood-damage, which officials estimated at $1.2 billion. More than 300 people were killed and thousands made homeless in June in the worst floods to hit Yemen in three decades.
"We are about to reach an agreement with Yemen to provide $35 million to help alleviate damages of the recent floods," Sud said.

On Tuesday the official Yemeni news agency Saba said the Bank's International Development Agency (IDA) had provided loans totalling some $483 million to Yemen in the past few years, of which $237 million so far had been used.

Yemen, where annual inflation is around 100 percent and unemployment is put at around 25 percent, is implementing an economic, financial and administrative reform programme agreed by the World Bank and International Monetary Fund.
The IDA makes interest-free loans to poor countries.
